name: Question 15
problem:
A particle $P$ is traveling along the $x$-axis with displacement $s(t)$ from a fixed origin $O$ given by

$$
s(t)=(t+1){e}^{-t},\,t\ge 0.
$$

Find the time at which the acceleration is zero, and find the value of the velocity at this moment.
worked_solution:
First, we calculate $v(t)$ by differentiating $s(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}((t+1){e}^{-t}) \\  & =-t{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we differentiate $v(t)$ to find $a(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-t{e}^{-t}) \\  & =(t-1){e}^{-t}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we put $a=0$ to find the time when the acceleration is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}0 & =(t-1){e}^{-t} \\ t-1 & =0 \\ t & =1\end{aligned}
$$

So the acceleration is zero when $t=1.$ To find the velocity at this moment, we substitute this back into $v(t)$ to get

$$
v(1)=-1\cdot {e}^{-1}=-\frac{1}{e}.
$$

Question 15
?

A particle P is traveling along the x-axis with displacement s(t) from a fixed origin O given by s(t)=(t+1)e−t,t≥0. Find the time at which the acceleration is zero, and find the value of the velocity at this moment.

a
t=1,v=−1e
b
t=12,v=12e
c
t=12,v=−1e
d
t=2,v=−2e2
e
t=1,v=1e2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we calculate v(t) by differentiating s(t): v(t)=dsdt=ddt((t+1)e−t)=−te−t

Now, we differentiate v(t) to find a(t): a(t)=dvdt=ddt(−te−t)=(t−1)e−t

Next, we put a=0 to find the time when the acceleration is zero: 0=(t−1)e−tt−1=0t=1

So the acceleration is zero when t=1. To find the velocity at this moment, we substitute this back into v(t) to get v(1)=−1⋅e−1=−1e.
